verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Whether an initiative is backed by real resources, staffing, or enforcement versus being merely aspirational is direct evidence of substantive newsworthiness.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Whether hard incident facts are surfaced plainly and early versus buried under reassurance language speaks to the substantive disclosure content a journalist would extract, not merely to style.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: This scores extraction/scraping damage to the document, a pure artifact of how the text was captured, with no plausible link to the substance of the release.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Presence of a boilerplate About/disclaimer footer is template furniture, not content, though a well-resourced comms operation that includes full boilerplate may also be the kind of organization that issues more substantively significant releases.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Whether the text presupposes an unrecapped earlier installment is a self-containedness/context-dependency property of the writing, not the substance itself, though being part of an ongoing serial story could plausibly also signal higher underlying stakes.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Whether the central fact is genuinely entering the record here versus rehashing already-announced material directly measures novelty, a core substantive component of newsworthiness.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: This is a raw count of digit characters, including phone numbers and footnote markers, with an explicit instruction not to judge informativeness; a pure orthographic tally unlikely to track genuine substantive quality.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Directly measures whether the release contains genuinely new findings or terms versus restating mission/values, core evidence of substantive newsworthiness.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores the structural extent of point-by-point rebuttal against a named outside party rather than whether the response is right or wise, but being the subject of a real controversy serious enough to warrant rebuttal could also signal genuinely higher-stakes underlying content.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Detects rote calendar/embargo/newswire-cycle phrasing such as quarter-end references or 'for immediate release', procedural furniture unlikely to track genuine substance.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Flags a routine, template statistical-bulletin format; by nature this marks habitual, expected content, which if anything predicts lower rather than genuinely better substantive newsworthiness.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Measures how much the text reads like retail advertising copy, with an explicit instruction not to judge the marketing's quality, a genre/format marker rather than news substance.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Directly measures the scale of real-world consequence across companies, industries, or regulatory regimes, a core substantive impact criterion for newsworthiness.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the release's actual content contains a hook (celebrity, humor, stunt) that would independently draw journalistic interest, a recognized substantive news value.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores formal newswire dateline/ticker conventions with an explicit instruction not to treat the formatting as evidence the news is more important, though paying for formal wire distribution plausibly correlates with more established organizations whose disclosures are also genuinely more consequential.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the release gives the audience something concrete and immediately actionable, a substantive utility criterion bearing on genuine newsworthiness.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether a recognizable celebrity or cultural institution genuinely extends the story's real-world reach beyond the routine corporate beat, a substantive prominence criterion.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Directly measures the size of the population genuinely affected by the change, a core substantive impact/magnitude criterion.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores density of numerical data with minimal narrative context, an explicit density measure ('do not judge accuracy or importance'), more a data-dump genre marker than substantive evidence.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores visible character-encoding corruption, a pure technical artifact of the capture pipeline, with the text itself instructing it must not be treated as evidence of the item's care or importance.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores the writing's register or authorial voice independent of whether it contains facts at all, a style marker, though an organization confident enough to write in a distinctive voice may also be the kind that discloses genuinely more substantive news.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the item carries real legal force such as filings or binding enforcement, a direct substantive-consequence criterion explicitly distinguished from the readability of the legal language.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether a specific, consequential dramatic incident involving danger, jeopardy, harm, or crime is actually recounted, a substantive stakes criterion.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores framing language marking the item as a forwarded/republished internal communication, a production-provenance marker, though an unpolished internal memo made public could also carry more candid substantive disclosure than a normal press release.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the release offers genuinely distinctive access to a person, place, or experience with concrete particulars, a substantive human-interest criterion.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Directly measures how concretely and checkably the release states what actually changed, core substantive content.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the item is anchored to genuine time-sensitive stakes such as a crisis, deadline, or live event versus timeless content, a substantive timeliness criterion.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the release states concretely what will change, for whom, and how, versus vague intentions, direct substantive specificity.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Measures whether the text is a coherent, complete announcement with an identifiable subject and supporting details versus a fragment or listicle, substantive completeness of the news item itself.
